full_judgment:
SM Emdadul Hoque, J: This appeal is directed against the Judgment and Order dated 22-2-2022 passed by the High Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal No.330 of 2014, allowing the appeal upon setting-aside the order dated 12-10-2014, passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No.17 of 2014, arising out of Artha Jari Case No.18 of 1999,(corresponding to Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 1987 and Title Suit No. 1 of 1999), dismissing the said Miscellaneous Case filed under Order XXI rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 read with section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. 

 2. Facts leading to the filing of the civil petition are that, present respondent No.2, Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Sangstha as petitioner filed a Miscellaneous Case No.15 of 1987 under article 33 of the "Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Sangstha Order, 1972" against the present respondent Nos.3-7 as opposite-parties, seeking recovery of a default amount of Taka 5,79,15,055.07. In the Miscellaneous Case, the present respondent No.5, as opposite-party No.3, appeared to contest the proceedings. Subsequently, that Miscellaneous Case was transferred to the Sub-Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 2nd Court, Dhaka for disposal and renumbered as Title Suit No.01 of 1999 and the suit was decreed on contest against the present respondent No.5 and ex-parte against others, decreeing the sum of Taka 1,30,38,004.51. As the judgment-debtor failed to repay the decretal amount, the present respondent No.2, as the decree-holder, filed Artha Execution Case No. 18 of 1999 on 6-10-1999, including three schedules of properties. 

 3. During the proceedings of the said execution case, the decree holder bank, on 24-1-2000, filed an application for passing necessary order to sale out 'A' scheduled properties through an auction and the application was allowed and subsequently, the auction was held and the highest bidder participated in the bid, offering amount of Taka 3,51,00,000. But on the objection of the decree holder, the Court further directed him to take necessary steps under section 33(4) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for a second auction. However, instead of taking necessary steps for a second auction, the judgment debtor filed an application under section 38 before the executing Court, praying for private negotiation. Subsequently, the judgment debtor No.3 filed an application to execute and register the sale deed and handover the possession of the land in favour of the nominated purchaser, Mr. Arifur Rahman, upon receiving the dues by pay order. The said application was allowed by the Court and thereby, directed to deposit the pay order. On 11-2-2013, an amount of Taka 25,00,00,000 was deposited before the executing Court. On 25-2-2013 decree holder was allowed to withdraw Taka 9,05,00,000 while Taka 14,95,00,000 by the defendant No.3. On 12-2-2003 the judgment-debtor No.3 filed an application before the executing Court praying for the acceptance of the pay order, executing the Boinama and transferring the possession of the land in favour of the purchaser. By Order No.101 dated 18-2-2013, the Artha Rin Adalat directed the decree-holder and judgment-debtor No.3 to submit the title documents on 25-2-2013, with necessary order to be passed, following the scrutiny of the submitted documents. On 25-2-2013, the decree-holder submitted an application seeking exemption from filing the title documents before the executing Court. Subsequently, on 27-2-2013, the executing Court directed the execution and registration of a Boinama. On 20-5-2014, the present respondent No.!, as a third-party petitioner, filed an application under Order XXI, Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure, read with section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, seeking to set-aside all orders passed in the Artha Execution Case, including the orders dated 25-2-2013 and 27-2-2013, through which the auction was approved and the sale certificate (Boinama) was registered. The said application gave rise to Miscellaneous Case No.17 of 2014. The present appellant, as opposite-party No. 3 in the case, filed an application under section 19(1)(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, read with Order VII, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, seeking rejection of the Miscellaneous Case filed by the third-party petitioner. Hence, the case. 

 4. Eventually, the Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka by its judgment and order dated 12-10-2014, dismissed the Miscellaneous case No.17 of 2014. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said order of dismissal present respondent No.1 preferred First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 330 of 2014 before the High Court Division. 

 5. The High Court Division, after hearing of the learned advocates and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, by its judgment and order dated 22-2-2022, allowed the appeal and set-aside the Judgment and Order dated 12-10-2014, passed by the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, 2nd Court, Dhaka, and directed to proceed with the execution case afresh by publishing auction notice in compliance of the provision of section 33(1) and 33(4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. 

 7. Mr. Sk. Md. Morshed, the learned Senior Advocate along with Mr. Mohammad Arshadur Rouf, Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that the Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Sangstha, as the decree-holder, filed Money Execution Case No.18 of 1999, arising out of Title Suit No.01 of 1999. In the said execution case, as per the provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, the auction was held and confirmed on 25-2-2013,_ and a Boinama was executed under the signature of the Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka, on 27-2-2013. An order for delivery of possession to the Certificate holder was issued on 18-5-2014, as per the provisions of Order XXI, Rule 95 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Subsequently, the auction purchaser, Arifur Rahman, acting on his own behalf and on behalf of two other purchasers, received possession of the scheduled property on 20-5-2014. As a result, the Artha Rin Adalat, 2nd Court, Dhaka, rightly rejected Miscellaneous Case No.17 of 2014, holding that no irregularities were found in the auction process or in the execution and registration of the Boinama being No.199 dated 27-2-2013 in Money Execution Case No.18 of 1999. However, the High Court Division, based on a misconceived view, allowed the appeal. Consequently, the Judgment and Order of the High Court Division warrants interference. 

 8. He also submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that the property had previously been leased to Khandakar Nazrul Islam, and that the lease had subsequently been cancelled. As a result, Nazrul Islam had no locus standi to file any application under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Therefore, the Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka, rightly rejected Miscellaneous Case No.17 of 2014. The Judgment and Order of the High Court Division totally failed to address this aspect which requires interference. 

 9. He further submits that the High Court Division, based on a misconceived interpretation of section 33(4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, allowed the appeal by setting aside the order regarding the acceptance of the auction purchaser and the registered sale deed, along with all subsequent steps taken by him through the executing Court. Therefore, the Judgment and Order of the High Court Division requires interference. 

 13. After perusal of the papers and documents on records, it appears that during the proceedings of the execution case, the decree-holder bank filed an application on 24-1-2000 seeking an order to sell the 'A' scheduled properties through an auction. The application was allowed, and the auction was subsequently held, with the highest bidder offering Taka 3,51,00,000. However, upon objection from the decree-holder bank, the Court directed the decree-holder to take necessary steps for a second auction under section 33(4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 to publish auction notice to sell the property through auction. Instead of initiating the auction as mandated, the judgment-debtor filed an application under section 38 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 before the executing Court, praying for private negotiation. 

 15. After considering all the orders passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in the execution case No.18 of 1999 [provided in the Index of Papers of the Concise Statement, listed No.4], it is observed that no auction was conducted in compliance with the mandatory provisions of sections 33(1) and 33(4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, despite the fact that such steps had been fixed as required for the sale of the judgment-debtor's property.  17. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case as discussed above and the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. it is our considered view that the High Court Division after proper appraisal of the facts and law and the decisions as referred rightly passed the judgment, thus, we find no reasons to interfere with the decision of the High Court Division. 

 However, the decree-holder Bank is at liberty to proceed with the case in accordance with law.
